notes.front: What is a T-network?
notes.back: A three-element network shaped like a T: two elements in series along the line, with one shunt element to ground between them.
notes.explanation: Which parts go in series and which in shunt decides whether it passes high or low frequencies.
notes.example: Like a pi-network turned inside out: one part to ground in the middle instead of one at each end.
notes.evidence: What is the frequency response of a T-network with series capacitors and a shunt inductor?

notes.front: What is a Pi-L network?
notes.back: A pi-network with an additional series inductor at its output.
notes.explanation: The pool gives greater harmonic suppression as the reason for adding the inductor.
notes.example: Like a transmitter’s pi-network output stage with one more coil in the line to the antenna.
notes.evidence: A Pi-network with an additional output series inductor

notes.front: What is a Chebyshev filter?
notes.back: A filter type with ripple in its passband and a sharp cutoff.
notes.explanation: It accepts some unevenness in the passband in exchange for a steeper edge.
notes.example: Like a road with small bumps along it that ends at a sheer cliff rather than a gentle slope.
notes.evidence: Which filter type has ripple in the passband and a sharp cutoff? A. A Butterworth filter B. An active LC filter C. A passive op-amp filter D. A Chebyshev filter

notes.front: What is an elliptical filter?
notes.back: A filter with an extremely sharp cutoff and one or more notches in the stop band.
notes.explanation: The notches in the stop band are what set it apart from the other filter shapes in the pool.
notes.example: Like a cliff-edge filter with extra deep holes dug just past the edge.
notes.evidence: Extremely sharp cutoff with one or more notches in the stop band

notes.front: What is a helical filter used for?
notes.back: It is the filter most often used as a band-pass or notch filter in VHF and UHF transceivers.
notes.explanation: The pool prefers it over Sallen-Key, swinging-choke and finite impulse response filters for that job.
notes.example: Like the tuned front end of a 2 m handheld, keeping out signals far from the band.
notes.evidence: Which of the following is most frequently used as a band-pass or notch filter in VHF and UHF transceivers? A. A Sallen-Key filter B. A helical filter

notes.front: What is a crystal lattice filter?
notes.back: A filter for low-level signals made using quartz crystals.
notes.explanation: The pool rejects the idea that it is a power supply filter or one made of lattice-shaped crystals.
notes.example: Like a narrow receiver filter built from several quartz crystals instead of coils and capacitors.
notes.evidence: A filter for low-level signals made using quartz crystals

notes.front: What is a cavity filter?
notes.back: A filter built from resonant cavities: spaces enclosed by conducting walls, with very high Q and a narrow bandpass.
notes.explanation: Resonant cavities can also handle relatively large amounts of power and be tuned very accurately.
notes.example: Like a finely tuned organ pipe for radio waves, ringing strongly at one frequency only.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 11, chapter 1, cavity resonators, p. 1-45
notes.evidence: Resonant cavities have a very high Q and can be built to handle relatively large amounts of power. Cavities with a Q value in excess of 30,000 are not uncommon. The high Q gives these devices a narrow bandpass and allows very accurate tuning.

notes.front: What is a duplexer?
notes.back: A device that lets a system use the same antenna for both transmitting and receiving.
notes.explanation: The pool’s 2 m repeater duplexer is built from cavity filters.
notes.example: Like a revolving door that lets people in and out through one doorway without collisions.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 11, chapter 1, waveguide junctions, p. 1-57
notes.evidence: Any device that performs both of these functions is called a DUPLEXER. A duplexer permits a system to use the same antenna for both transmitting and receiving.

notes.front: What does a filter’s shape factor measure?
notes.back: Its ability to reject signals in adjacent channels.
notes.explanation: It compares the bandwidth far down the filter’s skirts with the bandwidth near the top; a figure close to 1 means steep sides.
notes.example: Like judging a hedge by how sharply it cuts off the view next door, not by how flat its top is.
notes.evidence: Which of the following measures a filter’s ability to reject signals in adjacent channels? A. Passband ripple B. Phase response C. Shape factor

notes.front: What is a Hartley oscillator?
notes.back: A coil-and-capacitor oscillator whose feedback is taken from a tapped (or split) coil in the tank circuit.
notes.explanation: Each common oscillator is named after the person who designed it, and they differ in how they tap the feedback.
notes.example: Like tapping a spring partway along its length to feel its bounce.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 9, chapter 2, feedback signals, p. 2-9
notes.evidence: When an oscillator uses a tapped coil (view (B)) or a split coil (view (C)), it is referred to as a HARTLEY OSCILLATOR.

notes.front: What is a Colpitts oscillator?
notes.back: A coil-and-capacitor oscillator whose feedback is tapped between two capacitors in the tank circuit.
notes.explanation: The capacitors form a divider, and the feedback signal is taken from the point between them.
notes.example: Like the Hartley, but with the tap on a pair of capacitors instead of on the coil.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 9, chapter 2, feedback signals, p. 2-9
notes.evidence: The second method of coupling the feedback signal is to use two capacitors in the tank circuit and tap the feedback signal between them. This is shown in view (D). An oscillator using this method is referred to as a COLPITTS OSCILLATOR.

notes.front: What is a Pierce oscillator?
notes.back: A crystal-controlled oscillator, a modified Colpitts in which a quartz crystal replaces the parallel-resonant tank circuit.
notes.explanation: It works like a Colpitts, but the crystal acts as the parallel-resonant circuit.
notes.example: Like a Colpitts with its coil-and-capacitor tank swapped for a crystal.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 9, chapter 2, crystal-controlled Pierce oscillator, p. 2-27
notes.evidence: The Pierce oscillator is a modified Colpitts oscillator. They operate in the same way except that the crystal unit replaces the parallel-resonant circuit of the Colpitts.

notes.front: What is thermal drift in an oscillator?
notes.back: A change in frequency caused by temperature changing the values of components such as capacitors, resistors and transistors.
notes.explanation: Humidity changes components too; either way, amplitude and frequency shift with them.
notes.example: Like a guitar going out of tune as a cold room warms up.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 9, chapter 2, stability, p. 2-3
notes.evidence: As a result of changing temperature and humidity conditions, the value or characteristics of components such as capacitors, resistors, and transistors can change. The changes in these components also cause changes in amplitude and frequency.

notes.front: What job does the pool give NP0 capacitors in crystal oscillators?
notes.back: Reducing thermal drift.
notes.explanation: NP0 capacitors barely change value with temperature, so the frequency they help set stays put as the oscillator warms.
notes.example: Like choosing a steel ruler that barely grows in the heat for a measurement that must not change.
notes.evidence: Which of the following components can be used to reduce thermal drift in crystal oscillators? A. NP0 capacitors

notes.front: What is a microphonic in an oscillator?
notes.back: A change in oscillator frequency caused by mechanical vibration.
notes.explanation: Vibration reaching the oscillator’s parts shifts its frequency, which is why the cure is mechanical isolation.
notes.example: Like a mobile rig’s signal wobbling as the car hits potholes.
notes.evidence: Changes in oscillator frequency caused by mechanical vibration

notes.front: What is a crystal’s load capacitance?
notes.back: The specified parallel capacitance the crystal must see for the oscillator to run on the manufacturer’s stated frequency.
notes.explanation: The pool rejects parallel inductance, bias voltage or bias current as the way to set the frequency.
notes.example: Like a shoe size printed on a crystal’s data sheet: the circuit must fit it for the frequency to be right.
notes.evidence: Provide the crystal with a specified parallel capacitance

notes.front: What is a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO)?
notes.back: An oscillator whose frequency is steered by a DC control voltage.
notes.explanation: In an automatic frequency control circuit, a detector’s DC output proportional to the frequency error is applied to the oscillator.
notes.example: Like a car’s cruise control: a correction signal nudges the speed back to the set value.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 17, chapter 2, automatic frequency control, p. 2-28
notes.evidence: Our detector output is a dc control voltage proportional to the amount of frequency change. This dc voltage is applied directly to the oscillator.

notes.front: What is a phase-locked loop (PLL)?
notes.back: An electronic servo loop of a phase detector, a low-pass filter, a voltage-controlled oscillator and a stable reference oscillator.
notes.explanation: The loop steers the VCO so that it stays locked in phase with the stable reference.
notes.example: Like a runner matching stride to a pacemaker, speeding up or slowing down whenever they fall out of step.
notes.evidence: An electronic servo loop consisting of a phase detector, a low-pass filter, a voltage-controlled oscillator, and a stable reference oscillator

notes.front: What is a frequency synthesizer?
notes.back: A circuit that produces the frequencies it needs from stable references, reaching a stability a variable frequency oscillator cannot practically achieve.
notes.explanation: Many communications oscillators need long-term accuracy of one part in a million, beyond a VFO.
notes.example: Like a keypad-tuned transceiver whose every channel is as steady as its reference crystal.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 17, chapter 2, frequency synthesis, p. 2-29
notes.evidence: Variable frequency oscillators cannot practically achieve this high degree of stability. Therefore, a system known as FREQUENCY SYNTHESIS has been developed to meet the stringent demands for stability.

notes.front: In which kind of frequency synthesizer is a phase accumulator a building block?
notes.back: A direct digital synthesizer, alongside a lookup table, a digital-to-analog converter and a low-pass anti-alias filter.
notes.explanation: The pool names these four blocks as what makes a synthesizer a DDS rather than a PLL or hybrid type.
notes.example: Like the first of four carriages that together make up a DDS train.
notes.evidence: What type of frequency synthesizer circuit uses a phase accumulator, lookup table, digital-to-analog converter, and a low-pass anti-alias filter? A. A direct digital synthesizer

notes.front: What does the lookup table of a direct digital synthesizer hold?
notes.back: Amplitude values that represent the desired waveform.
notes.explanation: It holds the shape of the wave, not phase relationships or a list of operating frequencies.
notes.example: Like a table of sine values in a maths book, read out one entry after another.
notes.evidence: Amplitude values that represent the desired waveform

notes.front: In the simplest low-pass filter, where do the inductor and capacitor go?
notes.back: The inductor in series with the line; the capacitor across the line.
notes.explanation: The series coil opposes high frequencies while the capacitor bypasses them around the load.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 9, chapter 1, low-pass filter, p. 1-35
notes.evidence: By combining the series inductance and bypass capacitance, as shown in view (C), the simplest type of low-pass filter is obtained.

notes.front: In a simple high-pass filter, where do the capacitor and inductor go?
notes.back: The capacitor in series with the line; the inductor across the line.
notes.explanation: The series capacitor passes high frequencies, while the shunt inductor returns the low frequencies to the source.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 9, chapter 1, high-pass filter, p. 1-36
notes.evidence: most of the high-frequency energy is passed on to the load by the capacitor, and most of the low-frequency energy is shunted back to the source through the inductor.

notes.front: What three things does an oscillator need?
notes.back: Amplification; enough regenerative feedback to sustain oscillation; a frequency-determining device.
notes.explanation: These requirements, together with the application, determine the type of oscillator to be used.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 9, chapter 2, oscillator requirements, p. 2-3
notes.evidence: Second, sufficient regenerative feedback is required to sustain oscillations. Third, a frequency-determining device is needed to maintain the desired output frequency.

notes.front: What does the Navy course say about the frequency stability of a crystal-controlled oscillator?
notes.back: It is excellent, and the crystal oscillator is used from the middle of the audio range through the radio frequency range.
notes.explanation: The course sets it beside resistor-capacitor and coil-capacitor oscillators as a type of sine-wave generator.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 9, chapter 2, sine-wave oscillators, p. 2-2
notes.evidence: The crystal- controlled oscillator provides excellent frequency stability and is used from the middle of the audio range through the radio frequency range.

notes.front: How do transmitters that need very high frequency stability keep their crystals from drifting?
notes.back: They use thermostatically controlled ovens to hold the crystal at a constant temperature.
notes.explanation: Holding the temperature steady removes the cause of thermal drift.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 9, chapter 2, crystal-controlled oscillators, p. 2-24
notes.evidence: Transmitters which require a very high degree of frequency stability, such as a broadcast transmitter, use temperature-controlled ovens to maintain a constant crystal temperature.

notes.front: What is the primary difficulty with mixing-type frequency synthesizers, according to the Navy course?
notes.back: Spurious signals generated in the combining mixers.
notes.explanation: Extensive filtering and careful choice of operating frequencies are needed even in the simplest circuits.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 17, chapter 2, frequency synthesis, p. 2-29
notes.evidence: You will find the primary difficulty encountered in the frequency synthesizers is the presence of spurious signals generated in the "combining mixers."

notes.front: What long-term accuracy does the Navy course say many communications oscillators need?
notes.back: One part in a million.
notes.explanation: That is beyond a variable frequency oscillator, which is why frequency synthesis was developed.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 17, chapter 2, frequency synthesis, p. 2-29
notes.evidence: long term accuracy of one part in a million is required from many of the frequency generators (local oscillators) used in communications equipment.

notes.front: The major spectral impurities of a direct digital synthesizer are {{c1::spurious signals at discrete frequencies}}.
notes.explanation: The pool rejects broadband noise, conversion noise and local-oscillator harmonics as the main impurities.
notes.evidence: Spurious signals at discrete frequencies

notes.front: You want to pass 7 MHz from a transmitter but block its harmonics at 14 and 21 MHz. Which layout does it?
notes.choices:
A) Inductor in series with the line, capacitors across it
B) Capacitor in series with the line, inductor across it
C) Two capacitors in series with an inductor to ground between them
D) A single capacitor across the line only
notes.back: Inductor in series with the line, capacitors across it
notes.choicesExplained: B: series capacitor and shunt inductor make a high-pass filter, which would pass the harmonics. C: that is a high-pass T. D: the simplest low-pass filter combines series inductance with the bypass capacitance, not a capacitor alone.
notes.explanation: Harmonics are higher than the wanted signal, so a low-pass layout of series inductance and bypass capacitance is needed.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 9, chapter 1, low-pass filter, p. 1-35
notes.evidence: By combining the series inductance and bypass capacitance, as shown in view (C), the simplest type of low-pass filter is obtained.

notes.front: A T-network has two inductors in series along the line and a capacitor to ground between them. What is its response?
notes.choices:
A) Low-pass
B) High-pass
C) Band-pass
D) Notch
notes.back: Low-pass
notes.choicesExplained: B: high-pass needs series capacitors and a shunt inductor. C and D: those need resonant combinations, not single series and shunt elements.
notes.explanation: Series inductance opposes high frequencies and the shunt capacitor bypasses them: the low-pass arrangement.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 9, chapter 1, low-pass filter, p. 1-35
notes.evidence: By combining the series inductance and bypass capacitance, as shown in view (C), the simplest type of low-pass filter is obtained.

notes.front: A design needs the steepest possible cutoff and can accept notches in the stop band. Which filter type fits?
notes.choices:
A) Elliptical
B) Chebyshev
C) Butterworth
D) Helical
notes.back: Elliptical
notes.choicesExplained: B: Chebyshev has a sharp cutoff with passband ripple, but not stop-band notches. C: Butterworth is not the pool’s sharp-cutoff type. D: helical describes a VHF and UHF construction, not a response shape.
notes.explanation: An extremely sharp cutoff with one or more stop-band notches is the pool’s description of the elliptical filter.
notes.evidence: Extremely sharp cutoff with one or more notches in the stop band

notes.front: A coil-and-capacitor oscillator takes its feedback from a tap partway along its tank coil. Which type is it?
notes.choices:
A) Hartley
B) Colpitts
C) Pierce
D) Voltage-controlled oscillator
notes.back: Hartley
notes.choicesExplained: B: a Colpitts taps between two capacitors. C: a Pierce takes its feedback through a quartz crystal. D: a VCO is defined by its control voltage, not its feedback tap.
notes.explanation: A tapped or split coil is the Hartley’s way of coupling feedback.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 9, chapter 2, feedback signals, p. 2-9
notes.evidence: When an oscillator uses a tapped coil (view (B)) or a split coil (view (C)), it is referred to as a HARTLEY OSCILLATOR.

notes.front: A home-built VHF oscillator shifts frequency whenever the bench is knocked. What is the best fix?
notes.choices:
A) Mechanically isolate the oscillator from its enclosure
B) Fit NP0 capacitors
C) Increase the gain
D) Filter the power supply
notes.back: Mechanically isolate the oscillator from its enclosure
notes.choicesExplained: B: NP0 capacitors reduce thermal drift, not vibration. C: more gain does nothing for vibration. D: supply noise is not what knocks cause.
notes.explanation: Frequency shifts from vibration are microphonics, which the pool cures with mechanical isolation.
notes.evidence: Mechanically isolate the oscillator circuitry from its enclosure

notes.front: A crystal is marked for a particular load capacitance, but the builder’s oscillator gives it a different one. What happens?
notes.choices:
A) It will not run exactly on the marked frequency
B) It stops oscillating at once
C) It runs on an odd harmonic
D) Nothing changes
notes.back: It will not run exactly on the marked frequency
notes.choicesExplained: B: the pool ties the capacitance to the exact frequency, not to whether the crystal oscillates. C: the pool does not link load capacitance to harmonic operation. D: the specified parallel capacitance is what ensures the stated frequency.
notes.explanation: The pool makes the specified parallel capacitance the condition for running on the manufacturer’s frequency.
notes.evidence: Which of the following ensures that a crystal oscillator operates on the frequency specified by the crystal manufacturer? A. Provide the crystal with a specified parallel inductance B. Provide the crystal with a specified parallel capacitance

notes.front: Which block of a phase-locked loop produces the output frequency that the loop controls?
notes.choices:
A) The voltage-controlled oscillator
B) The phase detector
C) The low-pass filter
D) The reference oscillator
notes.back: The voltage-controlled oscillator
notes.choicesExplained: B: the phase detector compares phases; it makes no signal of its own. C: the filter smooths the control voltage. D: the reference stays fixed; it is what the loop locks to.
notes.explanation: The loop’s control voltage steers the VCO so its output stays locked to the stable reference.
notes.evidence: An electronic servo loop consisting of a phase detector, a low-pass filter, a voltage-controlled oscillator, and a stable reference oscillator

notes.front: In a direct digital synthesizer, which block turns the lookup table’s numbers into an analog signal?
notes.choices:
A) The digital-to-analog converter
B) The phase accumulator
C) The low-pass anti-alias filter
D) The phase detector
notes.back: The digital-to-analog converter
notes.choicesExplained: B: the phase accumulator comes before the lookup table. C: the filter cleans up the converter’s output. D: a phase detector belongs to a PLL, not a DDS.
notes.explanation: The lookup table holds amplitude values as numbers; turning numbers into a voltage is a digital-to-analog converter’s job.
notes.evidence: What type of frequency synthesizer circuit uses a phase accumulator, lookup table, digital-to-analog converter, and a low-pass anti-alias filter?

notes.front: A VHF receiver’s local oscillator must hold its frequency to about one part in a million over the long term. What should supply it?
notes.choices:
A) A frequency synthesizer
B) A free-running variable frequency oscillator
C) An astable multivibrator
D) A Hartley oscillator tuned by hand
notes.back: A frequency synthesizer
notes.choicesExplained: B: the Navy course says variable frequency oscillators cannot practically reach this stability. C: an astable multivibrator is a square-wave clock with limited stability. D: a hand-tuned oscillator is a variable frequency oscillator.
notes.explanation: Frequency synthesis was developed because such stability is beyond a variable frequency oscillator.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 17, chapter 2, frequency synthesis, p. 2-29
notes.evidence: long term accuracy of one part in a million is required from many of the frequency generators (local oscillators) used in communications equipment. Variable frequency oscillators cannot practically achieve this high degree of stability.

notes.front: A crystal oscillator creeps in frequency as the shack warms up each morning. Which change does the pool offer to reduce this?
notes.choices:
A) Use NP0 capacitors in the oscillator
B) Mechanically isolate the oscillator
C) Replace resistors with wirewound types
D) Use toroidal inductors
notes.back: Use NP0 capacitors in the oscillator
notes.choicesExplained: B: mechanical isolation cures microphonics, not temperature effects. C and D: wirewound resistors and toroidal inductors are the pool’s wrong options for thermal drift.
notes.explanation: A frequency change that follows temperature is thermal drift, and the pool names NP0 capacitors as a remedy.
notes.evidence: Which of the following components can be used to reduce thermal drift in crystal oscillators? A. NP0 capacitors

notes.front: How are the capacitors and inductors of a low-pass filter Pi-network arranged between the network’s input and output?
notes.choices:
A) Two inductors are in series between the input and output, and a capacitor is connected between the two inductors and ground
B) Two capacitors are in series between the input and output, and an inductor is connected between the two capacitors and ground
C) An inductor is connected between the input and ground, another inductor is connected between the output and ground, and a capacitor is connected between the input and output
D) A capacitor is connected between the input and ground, another capacitor is connected between the output and ground, and an inductor is connected between the input and output
notes.back: Capacitors from input and output to ground, with an inductor connected between input and output
notes.choicesExplained: A: that is a low-pass T, not a pi. B: series capacitors with a shunt inductor make a high-pass T. C: series capacitor with shunt inductors is a high-pass pi.
notes.explanation: The capacitors go from input and output to ground, with the inductor in series between them: series inductance and bypass capacitance, the low-pass layout.
notes.evidence: How are the capacitors and inductors of a low-pass filter Pi-network arranged between the network’s input and output?

notes.front: What is the frequency response of a T-network with series capacitors and a shunt inductor?
notes.choices:
A) Low-pass
B) High-pass
C) Band-pass
D) Notch
notes.back: High-pass
notes.choicesExplained: A: low-pass needs series inductors and a shunt capacitor. C and D: band-pass and notch need resonant combinations.
notes.explanation: Series capacitors pass high frequencies and the shunt inductor returns low frequencies to the source, so the network is high-pass.
notes.evidence: What is the frequency response of a T-network with series capacitors and a shunt inductor?

notes.front: What is the purpose of adding an inductor to a Pi-network to create a Pi-L-network?
notes.choices:
A) Greater harmonic suppression
B) Higher efficiency
C) To eliminate one capacitor
D) Greater transformation range
notes.back: Greater harmonic suppression
notes.choicesExplained: B: efficiency is not the gain. C: it adds a part rather than removing a capacitor. D: a greater transformation range is not the pool’s answer.
notes.explanation: The extra series inductor adds another low-pass section at the output, so harmonics, which lie above the wanted frequency, are attenuated further.
notes.evidence: What is the purpose of adding an inductor to a Pi-network to create a Pi-L-network?

notes.front: How does an impedance-matching circuit transform a complex impedance to a resistive impedance?
notes.choices:
A) It introduces negative resistance to cancel the resistive part of impedance
B) It introduces transconductance to cancel the reactive part of impedance
C) It cancels the reactive part of the impedance and changes the resistive part to the desired value
D) Reactive currents are dissipated in matched resistances
notes.back: It cancels the reactive part of the impedance and changes the resistive part to the desired value
notes.choicesExplained: A: it does not use negative resistance. B: transconductance is an amplifier property. D: dissipating power in resistors would waste it.
notes.explanation: Matching cancels the reactance and sets the resistance to the value wanted, leaving a purely resistive load.
notes.evidence: How does an impedance-matching circuit transform a complex impedance to a resistive impedance?

notes.front: Which filter type has ripple in the passband and a sharp cutoff?
notes.choices:
A) A Butterworth filter
B) An active LC filter
C) A passive op-amp filter
D) A Chebyshev filter
notes.back: A Chebyshev filter
notes.choicesExplained: A: a Butterworth has a flat passband with no ripple. B and C: “active LC” and “passive op-amp” describe construction, not this response.
notes.explanation: Passband ripple traded for a sharp cutoff is the Chebyshev’s signature.
notes.evidence: Which filter type has ripple in the passband and a sharp cutoff?

notes.front: What are the characteristics of an elliptical filter?
notes.choices:
A) Gradual passband rolloff with minimal stop-band ripple
B) Extremely flat response over its pass band with gradually rounded stop-band corners
C) Extremely sharp cutoff with one or more notches in the stop band
D) Gradual passband rolloff with extreme stop-band ripple
notes.back: Extremely sharp cutoff with one or more notches in the stop band
notes.choicesExplained: A and D: gradual rolloff is the opposite of an elliptical. B: an extremely flat passband with rounded corners is not its description.
notes.explanation: Notches in the stop band plus an extremely sharp cutoff describe the elliptical filter.
notes.evidence: What are the characteristics of an elliptical filter?

notes.front: Which describes a Pi-L network?
notes.choices:
A) A Phase Inverter Load network
B) A Pi-network with an additional output series inductor
C) A network with only three discrete parts
D) A matching network in which all components are isolated from ground
notes.back: A Pi-network with an additional output series inductor
notes.choicesExplained: A: the name does not mean “phase inverter load”. C: it has more than three parts. D: its capacitors go to ground.
notes.explanation: It is a pi-network with one more inductor in series at the output.
notes.evidence: Which describes a Pi-L network?

notes.front: Which of the following is most frequently used as a band-pass or notch filter in VHF and UHF transceivers?
notes.choices:
A) A Sallen-Key filter
B) A helical filter
C) A swinging choke filter
D) A finite impulse response filter
notes.back: A helical filter
notes.choicesExplained: A: a Sallen-Key is an active op-amp filter. C: a swinging choke belongs to power supply filters. D: a finite impulse response filter is a digital filter.
notes.explanation: A helical resonator gives high Q in a small, shielded can at VHF and UHF, where ordinary coils and capacitors are lossy, so it makes a compact, sharp band-pass or notch filter.
notes.evidence: Which of the following is most frequently used as a band-pass or notch filter in VHF and UHF transceivers?

notes.front: What is a crystal lattice filter?
notes.choices:
A) A power supply filter made with interlaced quartz crystals
B) An audio filter made with four quartz crystals that resonate at 1 kHz intervals
C) A filter using lattice-shaped quartz crystals for high-Q performance
D) A filter for low-level signals made using quartz crystals
notes.back: A filter for low-level signals made using quartz crystals
notes.choicesExplained: A: it is not a power supply filter. B: its crystals do not sit at 1 kHz intervals for audio. C: the crystals are not lattice-shaped; the name describes the circuit.
notes.explanation: Quartz crystals have very high Q, so several together make a narrow, steep-sided filter; they cannot handle much power, so it is used on low-level signals such as a receiver’s IF.
notes.evidence: What is a crystal lattice filter?

notes.front: Which of the following filters is used in a 2-meter band repeater duplexer?
notes.choices:
A) A crystal filter
B) A cavity filter
C) A DSP filter
D) An L-C filter
notes.back: A cavity filter
notes.choicesExplained: A: crystal filters work at low signal levels. C: a DSP filter works on digitised signals, not a transmitter’s RF path. D: ordinary L-C filters lack the cavity’s Q.
notes.explanation: Cavities have very high Q and can handle relatively large power, which suits a repeater duplexer.
notes.evidence: Which of the following filters is used in a 2-meter band repeater duplexer?

notes.front: Which of the following measures a filter’s ability to reject signals in adjacent channels?
notes.choices:
A) Passband ripple
B) Phase response
C) Shape factor
D) Noise factor
notes.back: Shape factor
notes.choicesExplained: A: passband ripple is flatness within the passband. B: phase response concerns delay, not rejection. D: noise factor describes noise added.
notes.explanation: Shape factor compares a filter’s bandwidth far down its skirts with its bandwidth near the top; the closer it is to 1, the steeper the skirts and the better nearby signals are rejected.
notes.evidence: Which of the following measures a filter’s ability to reject signals in adjacent channels?

notes.front: What are three common oscillator circuits?
notes.choices:
A) Taft, Pierce, and negative feedback
B) Pierce, Fenner, and Beane
C) Taft, Hartley, and Pierce
D) Colpitts, Hartley, and Pierce
notes.back: Colpitts, Hartley, and Pierce
notes.choicesExplained: A, B and C: Taft, Fenner and Beane are not oscillator circuits, and “negative feedback” would stop oscillation.
notes.explanation: Colpitts, Hartley and Pierce are the three the pool names; each is named after its designer.
notes.evidence: What are three common oscillator circuits?

notes.front: What is a microphonic?
notes.choices:
A) An IC used for amplifying microphone signals
B) Distortion caused by RF pickup on the microphone cable
C) Changes in oscillator frequency caused by mechanical vibration
D) Excess loading of the microphone by an oscillator
notes.back: Changes in oscillator frequency caused by mechanical vibration
notes.choicesExplained: A: it is not a microphone amplifier. B: RF pickup on a microphone cable is a different problem. D: oscillators do not load microphones.
notes.explanation: Mechanical vibration shaking an oscillator’s parts shifts its frequency.
notes.evidence: What is a microphonic?

notes.front: What is a phase-locked loop?
notes.choices:
A) An electronic servo loop consisting of a ratio detector, reactance modulator, and voltage-controlled oscillator
B) An electronic circuit also known as a monostable multivibrator
C) An electronic servo loop consisting of a phase detector, a low-pass filter, a voltage-controlled oscillator, and a stable reference oscillator
D) An electronic circuit consisting of a precision push-pull amplifier with a differential phase input
notes.back: An electronic servo loop consisting of a phase detector, a low-pass filter, a voltage-controlled oscillator, and a stable reference oscillator
notes.choicesExplained: A: a ratio detector and reactance modulator are FM parts. B: a monostable multivibrator is a one-shot. D: it has no push-pull amplifier.
notes.explanation: The loop compares the VCO with a stable reference in the phase detector, filters the result and uses it to steer the VCO.
notes.evidence: What is a phase-locked loop?

notes.front: How is positive feedback supplied in a Colpitts oscillator?
notes.choices:
A) Through a tapped coil
B) Through link coupling
C) Through a capacitive divider
D) Through a neutralizing capacitor
notes.back: Through a capacitive divider
notes.choicesExplained: A: a tapped coil is the Hartley. B: link coupling is not the Colpitts method. D: a neutralizing capacitor cancels feedback rather than supplying it.
notes.explanation: A Colpitts taps its feedback between two capacitors, which form a capacitive divider.
notes.evidence: How is positive feedback supplied in a Colpitts oscillator?

notes.front: How is positive feedback supplied in a Pierce oscillator?
notes.choices:
A) Through a tapped coil
B) Through link coupling
C) Through a neutralizing capacitor
D) Through a quartz crystal
notes.back: Through a quartz crystal
notes.choicesExplained: A: a tapped coil is the Hartley. B: link coupling is not the Pierce method. C: a neutralizing capacitor cancels feedback.
notes.explanation: The Pierce is a Colpitts with a quartz crystal in place of the resonant tank, so the feedback passes through the crystal.
notes.evidence: How is positive feedback supplied in a Pierce oscillator?

notes.front: Which of these functions can be performed by a phase-locked loop?
notes.choices:
A) Wide-band AF and RF power amplification
B) Frequency synthesis and FM demodulation
C) Photovoltaic conversion and optical coupling
D) Comparison of two digital input signals and digital pulse counting
notes.back: Frequency synthesis and FM demodulation
notes.choicesExplained: A: it is not a power amplifier. C: photovoltaic conversion and optical coupling are optoelectronics. D: comparing digital inputs and counting pulses are logic jobs.
notes.explanation: A PLL can lock an oscillator to a reference to synthesize frequencies, and it can track an FM signal to demodulate it.
notes.evidence: Which of these functions can be performed by a phase-locked loop?

notes.front: How can an oscillator’s microphonic responses be reduced?
notes.choices:
A) Use NP0 capacitors
B) Reduce noise on the oscillator’s power supply
C) Increase the gain
D) Mechanically isolate the oscillator circuitry from its enclosure
notes.back: Mechanically isolate the oscillator circuitry from its enclosure
notes.choicesExplained: A: NP0 capacitors reduce thermal drift. B: power-supply noise is a separate problem. C: more gain does not stop vibration effects.
notes.explanation: Microphonics come from vibration, so the cure is to keep vibration from reaching the oscillator.
notes.evidence: How can an oscillator’s microphonic responses be reduced?

notes.front: Which of the following components can be used to reduce thermal drift in crystal oscillators?
notes.choices:
A) NP0 capacitors
B) Toroidal inductors
C) Wirewound resistors
D) Non-inductive resistors
notes.back: NP0 capacitors
notes.choicesExplained: B, C and D: toroidal inductors and wirewound or non-inductive resistors are not the pool’s answer.
notes.explanation: NP0 capacitors have a temperature coefficient close to zero, so their value, and the frequency they help set, barely changes as the oscillator warms up.
notes.evidence: Which of the following components can be used to reduce thermal drift in crystal oscillators?

notes.front: What type of frequency synthesizer circuit uses a phase accumulator, lookup table, digital-to-analog converter, and a low-pass anti-alias filter?
notes.choices:
A) A direct digital synthesizer
B) A hybrid synthesizer
C) A phase-locked loop synthesizer
D) A direct conversion synthesizer
notes.back: A direct digital synthesizer
notes.choicesExplained: B: a hybrid synthesizer combines methods. C: a PLL synthesizer uses a phase detector and VCO. D: direct conversion describes a receiver type.
notes.explanation: A phase accumulator, lookup table, converter and anti-alias filter are the four blocks of a direct digital synthesizer.
notes.evidence: What type of frequency synthesizer circuit uses a phase accumulator, lookup table, digital-to-analog converter, and a low-pass anti-alias filter?

notes.front: What information is contained in the lookup table of a direct digital synthesizer (DDS)?
notes.choices:
A) The phase relationship between a reference oscillator and the output waveform
B) Amplitude values that represent the desired waveform
C) The phase relationship between a voltage-controlled oscillator and the output waveform
D) Frequently used receiver and transmitter frequencies
notes.back: Amplitude values that represent the desired waveform
notes.choicesExplained: A and C: phase relationships with oscillators describe a PLL, not the table. D: it does not store operating frequencies.
notes.explanation: The table holds the waveform’s amplitude values, which the converter turns into the output signal.
notes.evidence: What information is contained in the lookup table of a direct digital synthesizer (DDS)?

notes.front: What are the major spectral impurity components of direct digital synthesizers?
notes.choices:
A) Broadband noise
B) Digital conversion noise
C) Spurious signals at discrete frequencies
D) Harmonics of the local oscillator
notes.back: Spurious signals at discrete frequencies
notes.choicesExplained: A: broadband noise is not the major impurity. B: conversion noise is not the pool’s answer. D: local-oscillator harmonics are not the pool’s answer.
notes.explanation: A DDS builds its output from a limited number of stored amplitude steps, and the rounding errors repeat in a regular pattern, which shows up as spurs at discrete frequencies.
notes.evidence: What are the major spectral impurity components of direct digital synthesizers?

notes.front: Which of the following ensures that a crystal oscillator operates on the frequency specified by the crystal manufacturer?
notes.choices:
A) Provide the crystal with a specified parallel inductance
B) Provide the crystal with a specified parallel capacitance
C) Bias the crystal at a specified voltage
D) Bias the crystal at a specified current
notes.back: Provide the crystal with a specified parallel capacitance
notes.choicesExplained: A: parallel inductance is not the specification. C and D: crystals are not set by bias voltage or current.
notes.explanation: A crystal is specified for a particular parallel (load) capacitance; given that, it runs on its marked frequency.
notes.evidence: Which of the following ensures that a crystal oscillator operates on the frequency specified by the crystal manufacturer?

notes.front: Which of the following is a technique for providing highly accurate and stable oscillators needed for microwave transmission and reception?
notes.choices:
A) Use a GPS signal reference
B) Use a rubidium stabilized reference oscillator
C) Use a temperature-controlled high Q dielectric resonator
D) All these choices are correct
notes.back: All these choices are correct
notes.choicesExplained: A, B and C: each is a valid technique on its own, so the answer is all of them.
notes.explanation: Each ties the oscillator to something steadier than an ordinary crystal: GPS timing from satellite atomic clocks, a rubidium atomic reference, or a high-Q resonator held at a constant temperature.
notes.evidence: Which of the following is a technique for providing highly accurate and stable oscillators needed for microwave transmission and reception?

notes.front: How does the feedback tap of a Hartley oscillator differ from a Colpitts oscillator’s?
notes.back: Hartley: a tapped or split coil. Colpitts: the point between two capacitors.
notes.explanation: Both tap part of the tank circuit’s signal as feedback; they differ only in which tank component carries the tap.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 9, chapter 2, feedback signals, p. 2-9
notes.evidence: The second method of coupling the feedback signal is to use two capacitors in the tank circuit and tap the feedback signal between them.

notes.front: How does an elliptical filter’s response differ from a Chebyshev filter’s?
notes.back: Chebyshev: ripple in the passband and a sharp cutoff. Elliptical: an extremely sharp cutoff plus notches in the stop band.
notes.explanation: Stop-band notches are the elliptical’s distinguishing feature; passband ripple is the Chebyshev’s.
notes.evidence: Extremely sharp cutoff with one or more notches in the stop band

notes.front: What does a Pi-L network add to a pi-network, and what does that gain?
notes.back: An extra series inductor at the output, for greater harmonic suppression.
notes.explanation: The pool rejects higher efficiency, fewer capacitors and a greater transformation range as the purpose.
notes.evidence: What is the purpose of adding an inductor to a Pi-network to create a Pi-L-network? A. Greater harmonic suppression

notes.front: How is a PLL synthesizer built differently from a direct digital synthesizer?
notes.back: PLL: phase detector, low-pass filter, VCO and reference oscillator. DDS: phase accumulator, lookup table, digital-to-analog converter and anti-alias filter.
notes.explanation: One steers an oscillator into lock; the other builds the waveform from stored amplitude values.
notes.evidence: What type of frequency synthesizer circuit uses a phase accumulator, lookup table, digital-to-analog converter, and a low-pass anti-alias filter? A. A direct digital synthesizer B. A hybrid synthesizer C. A phase-locked loop synthesizer
